title: How to Spot a Fake Stock Certificate
summary: How to spot a fake stock certificate offered as KYB ownership evidence, when the ledger matters more than the vignette.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** A fake stock certificate is a share certificate edited after a real issuance, or generated to look engraved, offered as KYB ownership evidence when the issuer's books do not show those shares in that name.[31 CFR 1010.230](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1010/subpart-B/section-1010.230) requires a covered institution to identify each individual who owns 25 percent or more of the equity interests. An allegorical vignette does not establish that percentage.


## What a Fake Stock Certificate Actually Is


A stock certificate, also called a share certificate, is the issuer's evidence that a named person holds a stated number and class of shares registered in certificate form. A fake certificate makes that claim without a matching stock-ledger entry, or it presents a genuine certificate whose holder, count, class, or date changed after issuance.


The file arrives in two production families. Edited-after-creation starts from a real instrument, counsel's certificate, a cap-table export, or a scan of engraved paper, and then changes a field. Generated-from-scratch builds the border, the seal, the vignette, and the signature lines in a design tool or a generative model, with no issuance behind the page. Neither file is the stock ledger.


Neighboring documents get mislabeled as this one. A[certificate of incorporation](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-certificate-of-incorporation) attests that the corporation was formed and which classes are authorized. It does not name the holder of a numbered certificate. A[brokerage statement](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-brokerage-statement) is the carrying firm's account record. The SEC's July 2023[Investor Bulletin on holding securities](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-97) draws the line: street-name shares are registered to an intermediary, and the statement shows the customer as beneficial owner. A share certificate puts the holder's name on the issuer's own books.


[Delaware General Corporation Law § 158](https://delcode.delaware.gov/title8/c001/sc05/) sets the form. Shares are certificated unless the board resolves that some or all of a class or series will be uncertificated. Certificated shares entitle the holder to a certificate signed by any two authorized officers, and any or all of those signatures may be a facsimile. The corporation cannot issue a certificate in bearer form. A PDF with no holder, or one that says bearer, fails the statute before the vignette matters.


Most private-company certificates never see an intaglio press. Counsel issues a plain PDF: legal name, state, certificate number, holder, class, count, date, two signature blocks, and any legend the charter requires. An allegorical vignette on a young Delaware corporation is a style that issuer may never have used.[FinCEN's beneficial ownership page](https://www.fincen.gov/boi) records the registry gap. The August 11, 2026 final rule, effective August 14, 2026, exempts U.S. companies from beneficial ownership information reporting, so those shareholders are not in a federal database a reviewer can query.[UBO identification](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/what-is-ubo-identification) is that ownership or control judgment. The certificate is evidence for it, not the judgment itself.


## Tells That Still Work, and the Ones That Don't


A vignette can be copied. Holder, class, and count still have to match the issuer's ledger.


A blurry vignette, a crooked border, and a pixelated seal still catch a crude copy of an old engraved certificate. A genuine modern certificate often has no allegorical figure, and a generated certificate can show a cleaner vignette than a scan of intaglio ink. The border does not answer whether this corporation issued these shares to this person.


Facsimile signatures are the same trap. Section 158 allows any or all signatures to be a facsimile, and the certificate can remain valid after that officer has left office. Wet ink is not the test. A signature image sitting as its own object on a design-tool page is a production finding, not proof that every printed signature is forged.


Ledger tells still carry weight. The certificate number should be outstanding, in this holder's name, for this class and count, and not cancelled or replaced. The class has to exist in the certificate of incorporation. Words and figures have to name the same count, inside the shares the board issued. The name has to be the applicant, a disclosed owner, or an entity the chain already explains. A founder's certificate uploaded by someone else, with no assignment the ledger also shows, does not prove the uploader owns the shares.


Tell What it still catches What it misses


Blurry vignette, crooked border, pixelated seal Crude copies of engraved certificates A plain counsel PDF, and a generated page with a clean vignette


Expecting wet-ink signatures Almost nothing reliable Lawful facsimile signatures on a genuine certificate


Number, class, and count versus the ledger and charter Invented numbers, wrong class, inflated counts, cancelled certificates A real certificate the applicant does not own, until the ledger is checked


Same vignette, number, or template across applicants Serial reuse of one certificate A first-time generated file with a unique number


A match to a public specimen is not a pass. A file that still shows a specimen or cancelled mark is borrowing a picture of a certificate. The same vignette or number on a second unrelated application is a pattern one file cannot show.


## How Detection Actually Works


Six checks read how the file was made, when it changed, and whether the issuer's books agree.


Detection on a share certificate is the file's story, not a verdict on the vignette. Production method asks how the bytes were made. A counsel PDF, a cap-table export, a scan of security paper, a design-tool layout, and a generative page do not share a path. An engraved look inside a design-application file is a production finding. A plain law-firm PDF is not a fail because it has no vignette.


Timestamp trail asks whether file history fits the issue date on the face. Certificates are reprinted after loss or transfer, so an older date on a recently saved file is not automatically fake. The trail should look like issuance or a later reissue, not an edit that touched the holder or the share count after the rest of the page was finished. Edited-after-creation often leaves that sequence with the border untouched.


Issuer matching binds the page to this corporation's books. Legal name and state have to agree with the certificate of incorporation and the live state search. The officers or transfer agent have to be people the corporation authorized, and the certificate number has to be outstanding for this holder, class, and count. A state search that returns the corporation does not verify the certificate. Private companies often have no public ledger. Ask the secretary or the cap-table administrator. Do not treat the PDF as the ledger.


Consistency runs that test inward and across the packet. Words and figures, class, and par or no-par have to match the charter, and the count has to support the percentage the customer certified. The CDD rule lets the institution rely on the customer's ownership information unless facts reasonably call it into question, and verification under the rule is of identity. A challenged certificate is a reason to stop relying on the percentage. Generators produce that agreement by construction. Inconsistency is a fail. Consistency passes only when the issuer's records agree.


Model artifacts are what a generated page leaves when the engraving was never printed: synthetic vignette texture, a flat border, a seal as its own object, layout that neither intaglio nor a counsel template shares. Recycled patterns close serial reuse: one certificate number, vignette, legend, or signature image across applicants who do not share an issuer. Those six checks are classes of evidence, not a method for producing a cleaner certificate. A hidden ledger still needs a person.


## What to Do with a Suspect File


Stop treating the upload as the stock ledger. Confirm the class exists and that authorized shares can support the count. Compare holder, number, class, and issue date to the board consent, the cap table, and any ledger the secretary can produce. A missing, cancelled, or replaced number is a rejection as ownership evidence. If the board made the class uncertificated, paper is a contradiction until the issuer shows the shares were issued in certificate form.


When the books match and the file still looks edited, compare the native PDF with any screenshot and the file history with the printed date. The same number, vignette, or template on two unrelated applications is enough to hold both. Do not clear the second because the first already looked official.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can you tell if a stock certificate is fake?


Compare holder, certificate number, class, and share count to the stock ledger, the board issuance, and the certificate of incorporation. Competent fakes fail when a real certificate was edited after creation, when the page was generated with no issuance behind it, or when the same certificate appears for an unrelated applicant.


### Is a stock certificate the same as a certificate of incorporation?


No. A certificate of incorporation attests that the corporation was formed and which classes are authorized. A stock certificate says a named holder owns a stated number of shares in certificate form. A genuine formation filing does not prove that certificate was issued.


### How is a stock certificate different from a brokerage statement?


A stock certificate represents shares registered on the issuer's books in the holder's name. A brokerage statement is the carrying firm's account record, often for street-name shares registered to an intermediary. One document does not authenticate the other.


### Does every corporation have to issue a paper stock certificate?


No. Delaware lets the board make some or all classes uncertificated. A right to a physical certificate is state law, and some issuers no longer issue paper. A missing vignette is not a fake, and an engraved PDF is not proof the board issued certificated shares.


### Does an engraved vignette prove a stock certificate is genuine?


No. Allegorical vignettes belong to older security printing. Many genuine private-company certificates are plain counsel PDFs, and a generated file can imitate a vignette with no shares on the books. The ledger match is the check.
